title: FindingDispositionRecord
description: What a versioned policy profile says about ONE deterministic validator finding. A disposition is an opinion about a fact; it is never the fact. `evidence_ref` points AT the validator result and carries the status the validator produced — a disposition can never restate it as something else, and no disposition of any classification turns a FAIL into a PASS.

rule_id.description: Scanner rule id, e.g. CKV_AWS_338. Absent when the finding carries none — such findings are UNCLASSIFIED, because a baseline can only speak about rules it can name.

check.description: Wider than the validation packet's check list on purpose (spec-first stack build §6.5): a check that cannot be disposed of is an un-waivable hard block with no human route.

evidence_ref.description: The validator result this disposition is about. Immutable from the disposition's side.

status.description: Only failing or unverifiable evidence gets a disposition. A PASS needs no policy opinion, and SKIPPED/NOT_RUN are honest non-results already.

classification.description: DEFECT: the code is wrong under any reasonable policy; eligible for bounded repair. MISSING_DECISION: depends on a parameter nobody has chosen — routes to a human and must NEVER consume an LLM repair attempt. OUT_OF_SCOPE: the control does not apply to this workload class. UNSATISFIABLE: no code change can close it (e.g. S3 cannot log to itself). UNCLASSIFIED: the baseline has no opinion — blocking, because silence is not permission.
classification.$comment: UNSATISFIABLE replaced INAPPLICABLE in Block 4A: 'inapplicable' was ambiguous against OUT_OF_SCOPE, and the new name states the actual property.

proposed_action.description: What would address it. Advisory text; performing it is a separate, deterministic or human-approved act.

explanation.description: Why this classification. For a baseline-driven disposition this cites the baseline entry; it is never free-form model narration presented as fact.

parameter.description: For MISSING_DECISION: the specific decision required, so intake asks one focused question instead of guessing.

baseline_ref.description: Which profile version produced this disposition. Carried so an acceptance can be bound to it and invalidated when it changes.

proposed_by.description: 'baseline' = deterministic hash-bound lookup. 'default' = no entry matched, therefore UNCLASSIFIED. 'model' is deliberately ABSENT from this enum: a model may explain a finding but may never classify one, and closing the data route matters as much as forbidding the claim.
